findings.reason: as written the node implements an exclusion that leaves the section's own failure class uncovered for any SIGKILLed worker under a `squeue` wait, so the plan needs either a producer-gone arm for "probe cannot answer and no process of the run is alive" or an explicit statement that the exit-record gate is dropped when no process is alive, and it needs the matching test arm.
findings.text: s6 now limits producer-gone to "a probe that answered" and defers the unanswered case to `_the_probe_did_not_answer`, but that branch (reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1227-1229) fires only when `_exit_record_ends_the_current_attempt(record, ended_exit)` is true, and a worker killed without writing an exit record leaves `ended_exit` None, so the run falls through to the generic waiting row at :1250-1264 exactly as the incident's 15-hour false "working" reading did; arm 4 (plan.html:119) then endorses this fall-through as permanent ("classifies the run exactly as it does today"), which is the one path in §6 where a run with no live process and no scheduler job still reads as working

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `process_liveness.process_alive` (reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:13), `recovery_liveness._live_descendant` (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:419), `_the_probe_did_not_answer` (reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:372), the `squeue -h -j` read (reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:357), `resumption.sweep` (reckon/crew/resumption.py:1776) and `obligations.py`'s classification→duty mapping (:51, :1831) all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of the four arms is a single conjunction whose stated negative control falsifies it (removing the liveness clause fails the file-wait arm; removing the scheduler clause fails the squeue arm), and the paired removals are the two clauses arms 2 and 4 isolate.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate is a repository test file and the cited incident evidence lives under `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>/`, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `WAIT_PRODUCER_GONE_SECONDS` and `wait_probe_history` name mechanisms; no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches the new symbols.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the exclusion added to §6 hands the scheduler wait's dead case to a branch that also requires an exit record, so a worker that vanished without writing one still reads as waiting.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s6 delivers one classification (producer-gone) and the obligation it derives, with one test file.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s6 declares no depends-on and needs none: it extends `classify_pointer` and the obligation mapping in modules it already owns, and no other section's deliverable is its input.
